text: physics = "living" only: sound names for its hurt, its death and its idle sound, vanilla or "<pack>.<file>". false or nil: silent. entitySpec.sounds: ({ hurt: string ?, death: string ?, ambient: string ? } | false)?

title: EntitySpec.speed
text: How fast it goes, in blocks a second. A vehicle's top speed; a living body's walk at forward = 1, the game's own mob walk by default. entitySpec.speed: number ?

title: EntitySpec.step
text: physics = "vehicle" only: blocks it climbs without a jump; 1 by default. entitySpec.step: number ?

title: EntitySpec.think_every
text: define only. Seconds between two thinks of one body; one tick (0.05) by default, at most 60. The engine spreads the bodies over the ticks. entitySpec.think_every: number ?

title: EntitySpec.turn
text: physics = "vehicle" only: degrees a second it turns at speed; 90 by default. entitySpec.turn: number ?

title: Faces.all
text: `all` is one picture for all six faces, `side` for the four sides (`all` if left out), `top` and `bottom` the ends. faces.all: TextureRef ?, side: TextureRef ?, top: TextureRef ?, bottom: TextureRef ?

title: Faces.down
text: One face by its name; a face left out is `side`. faces.down: TextureRef ?, up: TextureRef ?, north: TextureRef ?, south: TextureRef ?, west: TextureRef ?, east: TextureRef ?

title: Faces.front
text: `front` is the side a facing block faces and `back` the other; a face left out is `side`. faces.front: TextureRef ?, back: TextureRef ?

title: Field.abs
text: field:abs() → Field

title: Field.at
text: This field read `dx, dy, dz` blocks away: `fields.water:at(1, 0, 0)` is the water east of here. field:at(dx: number, dy: number, dz: number) → Field dx dy dz

title: Field.clamp
text: field:clamp(low: number, high: number) → Field low high

title: Field.curve
text: Straight lines through `{ { input, output }, ... }`, inputs rising. field:curve(points: { { number } }) → Field points

title: Field.floor
text: field:floor() → Field

title: Field.gt
text: 1 where this is the larger, else 0. field:gt(other: Field | number) → Field other

title: Field.lt
text: 1 where this is the smaller, else 0. field:lt(other: Field | number) → Field other

title: Field.max
text: field:max(other: Field | number) → Field other

title: Field.min
text: field:min(other: Field | number) → Field other

title: Field.smooth
text: 0 at `from`, 1 at `to`, smooth between. `from` may be the larger. field:smooth(from: number, to: number) → Field from to

title: Field.sqrt
text: field:sqrt() → Field

title: Fx.particle
text: Shows particle `name` ("dust", "end_rod", "explosion", "firework", "flame", "note", "totem_of_undying") at `pos`, or at every point of a list. Each point reaches players in the room within 64 blocks of its origin in 3D, including the boundary, before spread or velocity. `count` (1) at each point in a box `spread` (0) out; or with `velocity`, one particle moving along it (`speed` 1 then, else 0). `

title: Game.biomes
text: Biomes of the pack's own: a vanilla biome with other colours and weather. game.biomes: Biomes

title: Game.block
text: Returns one block in this version's numbers, or nil for a name this game has no word for. game.block(name: string) → Block ? name

title: Game.blocks
text: The one table that *adds* to a version rather than reading it. game.blocks: Blocks

title: Game.entities
text: The kinds of entity: `define` a pack's own, `amend` the game's own, and read a kind of the game: a mob kind by either spelling (`game.entities.cow`, `game.entities.Cow`), a kind that is not a mob by its name (`game.entities.arrow`); nil where the game has none. It iterates every kind, including pack definitions: `for name, kind in game.entities do`. game.entities: Entities & { [string]: (EntityKin

title: Game.item
text: Returns an item this game has, or nil for a name it does not; never an error. game.item(name: string) → Item ? name

title: Game.items
text: Defines items of the pack's own, with a texture for clients from 1.21.4. game.items: Items

title: Game.recipes
text: What a crafting grid and a furnace make of a pack's items; recipes are added while the pack loads. game.recipes: Recipes

title: Game.sea_level
text: The y of this world's sea level. game.sea_level: number

title: Game.terrain
text: What this world's overworld is made of: `snow` and `steps`, as citadel.yml writes them; read-only, nil when there is no list. game.terrain: { snow: boolean ?, steps: { TerrainStep }? }?

title: Game.texture
text: Returns a new texture of width by height pixels, see-through until drawn on, for a pack's block or item. game.texture(width: number, height: number) → Texture width height

title: Game.version
text: This game's version, such as "a0.1.0". game.version: string

title: Game.world_height
text: How tall the world is in blocks: 128, or 256 for a 1.8.9 world. game.world_height: number

title: Generated.biome_at
text: Returns the biome name a column gets. generated:biome_at(pos: Vec3) → string ? pos

title: Generated.sample
text: Returns a field's value at a position; `nil` for a field made after `world.generate`, or for rules with no `height`. generated:sample(field: Field | number, pos: Vec3) → number ? field pos

title: GeneratorRules.biomes
text: `{ "desert", when = field }`: the first that holds names the column's biome; one with no `when` is for the rest. generatorRules.biomes: { { [number]: string, when: (Field | number)? } }?

title: GeneratorRules.carvers
text: The game version's own carvers, with the world seed, after the land and before the cave rules: "caves" (every version), "ravines" (b1.8 and later). Needs `height` or `density`. generatorRules.carvers: { "caves" | "ravines" }?

title: GeneratorRules.density
text: Solid where this is above 0, for caves, overhangs and land in the air. generatorRules.density: Field ?

title: GeneratorRules.floor
text: The block at y 0; "bedrock" for a land of its own. generatorRules.floor: string ?

title: GeneratorRules.fluid
text: generatorRules.fluid: string ?

title: GeneratorRules.fluids
text: What fills the caves: needs `density` or `carvers`. generatorRules.fluids: { FluidRule }?

title: GeneratorRules.height
text: The y of the surface. generatorRules.height: (Field | number)?

title: GeneratorRules.plants
text: generatorRules.plants: { PlantRule }?

title: GeneratorRules.rock
text: The body of the land, under the ground rules. generatorRules.rock: { GroundRule }?

title: GeneratorRules.sea
text: Water fills the open air up to this y. generatorRules.sea: number ?

title: GeneratorRules.structures
text: The game version's own structures, with spawners and loot: "mineshaft", "dungeon" (1.7 to 1.12). Needs `height` or `density`. generatorRules.structures: { "mineshaft" | "dungeon" }?

title: GeneratorRules.surface
text: generatorRules.surface: { GroundRule }?

title: GeneratorRules.things
text: generatorRules.things: { ThingGrid }?

title: Hit.block
text: The block, when the click hit one. hit.block: Vec3 ?

title: Hit.button
text: "left" is an attack or swing, "right" is an interact or use. hit.button: "left" | "right"

title: Hit.entity
text: The thing clicked, as the handle the script holds for it. hit.entity: (Display | Hitbox | Npc | Puppet)?

title: Hit.entity_id
text: Its raw entity id, which is all there is for something the engine made itself, such as one of a screen's own frames. hit.entity_id: number ?

title: Hit.face
text: The face of the block that was clicked. hit.face: Face ?

title: Hit.player
text: Another player, when that is what was clicked. hit.player: Player ?

title: Hit.slot
text: The hotbar slot in hand, 1..9. hit.slot: number

title: Hitbox.at
text: Its bottom centre; write it to move the hitbox, and its wall when solid. hitbox.at: Vec3

title: Hitbox.destroy
text: Removes the hitbox, and its wall when solid. hitbox:destroy()

title: Hitbox.id
text: Its entity id, what `players.on_click` reports in `hit.entity_id`. hitbox.id: number

title: HttpResponse.body
text: The answer as bytes. httpResponse.body: string

title: HttpResponse.error
text: Why no answer came, or nil. httpResponse.error: string ?

title: HttpResponse.headers
text: The answer's headers, names in lower case. httpResponse.headers: {[string]: string }

title: HttpResponse.image
text: A PNG body: `pixels` is 4 bytes (RGBA) a pixel, row by row from the top. httpResponse:image() → {width: number, height: number, pixels: buffer}

title: HttpResponse.json
text: The body as a table; an error when it is not JSON. httpResponse:json() → any

title: HttpResponse.ok
text: True for a 2xx status. httpResponse.ok: boolean

title: HttpResponse.status
text: The HTTP status; 0 when no answer came. httpResponse.status: number

title: Hud.destroy
text: Takes it off the player's screen. hud:destroy()

title: Hud.set
text: A value per id: a number is a fill, a string a label's words, true or false whether it shows. An unknown id is an error that lists the ids. hud:set(values: { [string]: number | string | boolean }) values

title: HudPart.color
text: A box's colour, a picture's tint, a label's ink; reads back as "#rrggbb". hudPart.color: Ink ?

title: HudPart.fill
text: How much of a box or picture shows, from its left edge: 0 to 1. hudPart.fill: number

title: HudPart.text
text: A label's words. hudPart.text: string

title: HudPart.visible
text: Whether it shows; nil shows it again. hudPart.visible: boolean ?

title: ItemMeta.canvas
text: A filled map of that canvas: what the item *is*, so `item` may be left out. Everywhere an item is taken — a hand, a hotbar slot, a display. itemMeta.canvas: Canvas ?

title: ItemMeta.color
text: A potion's liquid colour; 1.11 and later. itemMeta.color: Color ?

title: ItemMeta.count
text: How many in the stack; 1 by default. itemMeta.count: number ?

title: ItemMeta.damage
text: The wear a tool has taken; 0 is new. itemMeta.damage: number ?

title: ItemMeta.dye
text: Leather armour's colour. itemMeta.dye: Color ?

title: ItemMeta.glint
text: The enchanted shine, with no enchantment. itemMeta.glint: boolean ?

title: ItemMeta.id
text: A pack's own item: a brick with `id = "copper_ingot"` is a copper ingot, kept under the pack's name and known by it everywhere it goes. itemMeta.id: string ?

title: ItemMeta.lore
text: One line or a list of lines, grey unless they say otherwise. itemMeta.lore: ({ Text } | Text)?

title: ItemMeta.model
text: The item model a 1.21.4+ client draws: `assets/<pack>/items/<model>.json`. itemMeta.model: string ?

title: ItemMeta.name
text: Never italic unless it says so. itemMeta.name: Text ?

title: ItemMeta.skin
text: The face a "player_head" item shows: a player's name, or the raw `textures` property. On any other item it is an error. itemMeta.skin: (string | { value: string, signature: string ? })?

title: Items.define
text: Load-time only. Hands back the item table: give it, match it, craft it. items.define(spec: { name: string, texture: TextureRef ?, label: Text ?, lore: ({ Text } | Text)?, looks: string ?, stack: number ?, glint: boolean ?, }) → ItemTable spec

title: Material.burns
text: Whether the jar's Material burns. material.burns: boolean

title: Material.covers
text: Grass under it dies. material.covers: boolean

title: Material.firm
text: Snow and ice need it beneath them. material.firm: boolean

title: Material.liquid
text: Whether the jar's Material is a liquid. material.liquid: boolean

title: Material.solid
text: Whether the jar's Material counts as solid. material.solid: boolean

title: Menu.destroy
text: Takes it down and forgets its callbacks. A Bedrock form cannot be taken back: it stays until the player answers, and the answer then lands nowhere. menu:destroy()

title: Menu.update
text: New pictures in place, the menu left open: a bar that fills, a count that changes. `on_pick` still answers by position. `false` once the player has put it away; a Bedrock form keeps what it showed. menu:update(items: { ItemSpec }) → boolean items

title: Model.name
text: The name the model was given in `models.new`. model.name: string

title: ModelBuild.animation
text: `{ length = seconds, loop = false, <part name> = { rotation = { [t] = is both named fields and part names, so this one is open. modelBuild:animation(name: string, opts: { [string]: any }) name opts

title: ModelBuild.material
text: Makes a named colour a display may repaint; `grain` (0 to 1) darkens pixels into four tones, `alpha` below 1 is glass. modelBuild:material(name: string, color: Ink, opts: { grain: number ?, alpha: number ? }?) → ModelMaterial name color opts

title: ModelBuild.part
text: Makes a named child part of the root that turns around its `pivot`, the model's origin unless given. modelBuild:part(name: string, opts: { pivot: Vec3 ? }?) → ModelPart name opts

title: ModelBuild.texture
text: Makes a pixel picture for one face; with `tint`, drawn in greys and coloured by that material. With `scroll`, it moves by itself on a block drawn from the model, `speed` texels a tick (1, 2, 3, or 0.5, 0.25). modelBuild:texture(width: number, height: number, opts: { tint: ModelMaterial ?, scroll: ("up" | "down" | "left" | "right")?, speed: number ? }?) → ModelTexture width height opts

title: ModelDisplay.destroy
text: Removes the model from the room. modelDisplay:destroy()

title: ModelDisplay.id
text: What `player:ride(model)` is handed; the seat is picked from `seats`. modelDisplay.id: number

title: ModelDisplay.move
text: Place and turn it in one step, every part and seat together. modelDisplay:move(at: Vec3, rotation: Orientation ?) at rotation

title: ModelDisplay.paint
text: Whether it is still present. Read-only. Where it stands; live, and each write is a move of its own. Partial writes preserve other angles; nil after removal. Reads vec3; write a number or equal-axis vec3 for uniform size. Nil when gone. Material name to colour; write-only. modelDisplay.paint: { [string]: Ink }

title: ModelDisplay.play
text: Starts an animation; replaying the current one changes speed without restarting. modelDisplay:play(animation: string, opts: { speed: number ? }?) animation opts

title: ModelDisplay.stop
text: Where it is; the parts stay as they are. modelDisplay:stop(animation: string) animation

title: ModelMaterial.name
text: The name it was made with, which a display repaints it by. modelMaterial.name: string

title: ModelPart.box
text: Corners in any order; a box turns on one axis, in steps of 22.5 up to 45, and `pivot` is the box's own centre unless you give one. modelPart:box(from: Vec3, to: Vec3, skin: ModelSkin, opts: { rotation: Vec3 ?, pivot: Vec3 ?, faces: { [Face]: ModelSkin }?, }?) from to skin opts

title: ModelPart.hitbox
text: A box a player can hit on a living body that wears the model (clients from 1.19.4). Not drawn; corners in any order, in model units. Square from above (its longer side), so split a long part. Animations do not move it. A model with none is hit on one box of the body's `size`. modelPart:hitbox(from: Vec3, to: Vec3) from to

title: ModelPart.mirror
text: A mirrored copy of every box and hitbox this part has, and a mirrored twin named `<name>_mirrored` of every child. Only "x" in this version. modelPart:mirror(axis: "x") axis

title: ModelPart.part
text: Makes a child part of this one; it turns around `pivot`, the model's origin unless you give one. modelPart:part(name: string, opts: { pivot: Vec3 ? }?) → ModelPart name opts

title: ModelTexture.fill
text: Paints every pixel one colour. modelTexture:fill(color: Ink) color

title: ModelTexture.pixel
text: Paints the pixel at x, y; `colors.transparent` makes it see-through. modelTexture:pixel(x: number, y: number, color: Ink) x y color

title: ModelTexture.rect
text: Paints a rectangle `w` by `h` pixels from x, y. modelTexture:rect(x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number, color: Ink) x y w h color

title: NetworkInstance.id
text: The instance's name. `player:connect` takes it. networkInstance.id: string

title: NetworkInstance.label
text: networkInstance.label: string

title: NetworkInstance.member
text: networkInstance.member: string

title: NetworkInstance.meta
text: The instance's own value. networkInstance.meta: any

title: NetworkInstance.open
text: The number of players it takes now, as it said with `network.status`. networkInstance.open: number ?

title: NetworkInstance.players
text: The number of players on it. networkInstance.players: number ?

title: NetworkInstance.state
text: "starting", then "online", then "stopping". networkInstance.state: string

title: NetworkInstance.status
text: The instance's own word. networkInstance.status: string ?

title: NetworkStarted.id
text: networkStarted.id: string

title: NetworkStarted.state
text: "starting" or "online". networkStarted.state: string

title: Noise.get
text: Returns about -1..1 at a point: `get(x, z)` for a height map, `get(x, y, z)` for caves and overhangs. noise:get(x: number, y_or_z: number, z: number ?) → number x y_or_z z

title: Noise.grid
text: Returns `width * depth` heights in one call, row by row: the number for `(x + dx, z + dz)` is at `[dz * width + dx + 1]`. noise:grid(x: number, z: number, width: number, depth: number) → { number } x z width depth

title: Npc.destroy
text: npc:destroy()

title: Npc.dismount
text: Gets off where it sits; set `at` after it to put it somewhere else. npc:dismount()

title: Npc.hold
text: Puts an item in the main hand; nil or false empties it. An error on an unknown item. npc:hold(item: (ItemSpec | false)?) item

title: Npc.id
text: The entity id, what `players.on_click` reports in `hit.entity_id`. npc.id: number

title: Npc.look_at
text: Where it stands; live, so setting it moves the NPC. A riding NPC reads the seat's position. Partial writes preserve other angles; nil after removal. Bodies have no roll. Turns head and body toward a point. npc:look_at(pos: Vec3) pos

title: Npc.move
text: Removes the NPC. Sets position and optional rotation together. npc:move(at: Vec3, rotation: BodyRotation ?) at rotation

title: Npc.name
text: Whether it is still present. Read-only. "" for one made with no name, which has no name tag. npc.name: string

title: Npc.pose
text: How the body is held; live. npc.pose: NpcPose

title: Npc.ride
text: Sits in a seat as `player:ride` does, and never drives; `false` when somebody sits there. npc:ride(thing: MountTarget, opts: { seat: number ? }?) → boolean thing opts

title: Npc.riding
text: Whether it sits in a seat; live. npc.riding: boolean

title: Npc.say
text: Sends a chat line "<name> ..." to the room, or just the words for an NPC with no name. npc:say(text: Text, color: Ink ?) text color

title: Npc.swing
text: Plays the arm swing animation. npc:swing()

title: Npc.walk
text: Walks the points by itself, facing where it goes; nil stops it. npc:walk(opts: { path: { Vec3 }, speed: number ?, loop: boolean ? }?) opts

title: Npc.walking
text: True while it walks a path, until the last point; never false with `loop`. npc.walking: boolean

title: Npc.wear
text: Puts armour on it, head first; each piece is an item. npc:wear(pieces: Worn) pieces

title: Overlay.destroy
text: Takes it off the player's screen. overlay:destroy()

title: Overlay.open
text: True until `destroy` or the player leaves. overlay.open: boolean

title: PartDefinition.at
text: Where the build's block (0, 0, 0) lands. partDefinition.at: Vec3

title: PartDefinition.build
text: Exactly a world.build function. partDefinition.build(b: Builder) b

title: PartDefinition.detail
text: 1 (whole blocks, the default) or 2 (half blocks), as world.build. partDefinition.detail: number ?

title: PartDefinition.name
text: Unique; a path, "downtown/tower-3", nests. partDefinition.name: string

title: Picture.circle
text: Fills a circle of radius `r` pixels around (x, y). picture:circle(x: number, y: number, r: number, color: Ink) x y r color

title: Picture.clear
text: Its width in pixels: 128 for each map across. Its height in pixels: 128 for each map down. Paints every pixel one colour; black by default. On a view, the default clears it to see-through. picture:clear(color: Ink ?) color

title: Picture.draw
text: Draws another screen, canvas or view with its top-left at (x, y), skipping its transparent pixels. picture:draw(source: Screen | Canvas | View, x: number ?, y: number ?) source x y

title: Picture.fill
text: Fills a w by h box of pixels with one colour, its top-left at (x, y). picture:fill(x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number, color: Ink) x y w h color

title: Picture.gradient
text: Fills a box that fades from `from` to `to`, top to bottom; `"across"` runs it left to right. picture:gradient(x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number, from: Ink, to: Ink, across: string ?) x y w h from to across

title: Picture.line
text: Draws a smoothed line with round ends, `width` pixels wide (1 by default); positions may be fractions. picture:line(x0: number, y0: number, x1: number, y1: number, color: Ink, width: number ?) x0 y0 x1 y1 color width

title: Picture.measure
text: The width in pixels that `text` would draw, without drawing it; for centring. picture:measure(text: string, size: number ?) → number text size

title: Picture.part
text: One map of the picture, `{ id = .. }`, by column and row from (0, 0) top- left; for a hand or a single frame. picture:part(col: number, row: number) → { id: number } col row

title: Picture.pixels
text: Writes raw RGB bytes (a buffer or a string), three a pixel, row by row, into a w by h box. picture:pixels(x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number, data: buffer | string) x y w h data

title: Picture.play
text: Plays a raw RGB video file from the pack at `fps` 0.5 to 20, the engine drawing each frame; returns the Video. picture:play(opts: { file: string, fps: number ?, loop: boolean ? }) → Video opts

title: Picture.polygon
text: Fills a smoothed shape with any number of corners; a point is `{x, y}` or `{ x = .., y = .. }`. picture:polygon(points: { { number } | { x: number, y: number } }, color: Ink) points color

title: Picture.rect
text: Fills a box like `fill`, with smoothed rounded corners of `radius` pixels when given. picture:rect(x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number, color: Ink, radius: number ?) x y w h color radius

title: Picture.ring
text: Draws a circle's outline, `width` pixels wide (1 by default), smoothed. picture:ring(x: number, y: number, r: number, color: Ink, width: number ?) x y r color width

title: Picture.set
text: Paints one pixel; (0, 0) is the top-left. picture:set(x: number, y: number, color: Ink) x y color

title: Picture.sprite
text: Draws pixel art: each string a row, each character a dot `scale` pixels square (1 by default); a character with no ink is skipped. picture:sprite(x: number, y: number, rows: { string }, inks: { [string]: Ink }, scale: number ?) x y rows inks scale

title: Picture.text
text: Draws text in DejaVu Sans Bold, `size` pixels tall (16 by default), smoothed; returns its width in pixels. picture:text(x: number, y: number, text: string, color: Ink, size: number ?) → number x y text color size

title: PlantRule.afloat
text: On the water over a column, not on its ground. plantRule.afloat: boolean ?

title: PlantRule.biome
text: plantRule.biome: string ?

title: PlantRule.block
text: plantRule.block: BlockPick ?

title: PlantRule.blocks
text: The blocks from the foot up, in place of `block`: a two-block flower. plantRule.blocks: { BlockPick }?

title: PlantRule.chance
text: plantRule.chance: (Field | number)?

title: PlantRule.clear
text: Blocks of water to keep clear over a plant that grows in it. plantRule.clear: number ?

title: PlantRule.height
text: How many blocks a plant that grows is tall: `block` repeats. plantRule.height: (Field | number)?

title: PlantRule.place
text: Where it goes: "top" (the default), or in the caves `density` or `carvers` dig: "floor", "ceiling" (it hangs down: `tip` is lowest) or "wall" (one block; `{wall}` in its name is the side the rock is on, `{facing}` the side away). title: PlantRule.sink

title: PlantRule.tip

title: PlantRule.when
text: plantRule.when: (Field | number)?

title: PlantRule.y

title: Player.add_group
text: Puts the player in a group until they leave; errors on a group citadel.yml does not define. player:add_group(group: string) group

title: Player.camera
text: What they look out of: a camera from camera.fixed/free/orbit/chase, or nil or false for their own eyes. No delay is needed after creating its target. Ends when the target is destroyed or the player leaves the room. player.camera: (Camera | false)?

title: Player.can_fly
text: May fly in a mode that cannot. player.can_fly: boolean

title: Player.can_see
text: True unless `other` is not visible or is hidden from this player. player:can_see(other: Player) → boolean other

title: Player.clear_effect
text: Takes a potion effect off the player, by its modern name. player:clear_effect(name: string) name

title: Player.connect
text: Asks Minefort to move the player to another server by name: an instance's `id`, the network's name (its default member) or "hub". Minefort decides and does not answer; a player still here was not moved. player:connect(server: string) server

title: Player.count
text: Returns how many of an item the player carries, across every slot. player:count(item: ItemMatch) → number item

title: Player.damage
text: A hit in half-hearts: the flash, the sound, the resistance window. `false` on a version with no damage rules. player:damage(amount: number) → boolean amount

title: Player.dismount

text: Tells after a mob died; it is gone, so its id and name is all there is. Mob kinds only. world.on_entity_death(fn: (id: number, name: string) -> ()) → Connection fn

title: World.on_entity_spawn
text: Tells after a mob appeared, with its handle and name; a natural spawn fires it on every game version that has one, and a pack's own `world.spawn("cow", pos)` fires it too. Mob kinds only. world.on_entity_spawn(fn: (entity: EntityHandle, name: string) -> ()) → Connection fn

title: World.on_generate
text: Called for a chunk each time it comes into memory, in a script world; it must make the same blocks every time. world.on_generate(fn: (chunk: Chunk) -> ()) fn

title: World.on_populate
text: Each chunk the overworld terrain made, once, after it made it. world.on_populate(fn: (chunk: Chunk) -> ()) fn

title: World.paste
text: Live, stored and sent; air is skipped unless `air` is true. world.paste(schem: Schematic, origin: Vec3, opts: { air: boolean ?, part: string ? }?) schem origin opts

title: World.path
text: The points a body walks from `from` to the block at `to`, or nil. The game's own search: a step up of one block, falls of `fall` (3). `size` is { width, height } (0.6, 1.8); `swim` goes through water; `range` (the distance + 16) and `budget` (2000 nodes) stop a long search, which then gives the part that came closest. world.path(from: Vec3, to: Vec3, opts: { size: (number | { number })?, swim: boo

title: World.puppet
text: Places a mob's body with no mind of its own that the script moves; its name tag always shows. An error when this game has no such mob kind. world.puppet(opts: { kind: string, at: Vec3 ?, rotation: BodyRotation ?, name: Text ? }) → Puppet opts

title: World.raycast
text: The first block a ray from `from` along `direction` meets within `max` blocks, and the face it came in through; nil for none. world.raycast(from: Vec3, direction: Vec3, max: number ?) → RayHit ? from direction max

title: World.raycasts
text: `n` lines at once. `rays` holds six f64 a line (from x, y, z, to x, y, z); `out` gets one f64 a line: how far along it the first block is that stops it, or -1 for a clear line. world.raycasts(rays: buffer, out: buffer, n: number) rays out n

title: World.rules
text: `world.rules{ fall = true }` switches one on, false off; a rule left out or nil keeps its value, and a number or a string is an error. `world.rules()` reads them. world.rules(opts: { survival: boolean ?, fall: boolean ?, damage: boolean ?, hunger: boolean ?, anticheat: boolean ?, day_cycle: boolean ?, redstone: boolean ? }?) → Rules opts

title: World.schematic
text: A file inside the pack; a path that leaves it, or one that is not there, is an error naming the file. world.schematic(file: string) → Schematic file

title: World.screen
text: Puts a wall of map frames, `width` by `height` frames (128 pixels each), in front of a wall; `at` is the top-left frame. Returns a Screen. world.screen(opts: { at: Vec3, facing: Facing | "up", up: Facing ?, width: number ?, height: number ?, glow: boolean ?, on_click: ((player: Player, x: number, y: number, button: "left" | "right") -> ())?, }) → Screen opts

title: World.sees
text: True when no block stops the line from `from` to `to`: a block with a collision box does (glass, leaves), water and grass do not. world.sees(from: Vec3, to: Vec3) → boolean from to

title: World.set_block
text: `skin` is for "player_head" and "player_wall_head" only: an account's name, or the raw `textures` property. world.set_block(pos: Vec3, block: BlockRef, opts: { skin: HeadSkin ? }?) pos block opts

title: World.set_blocks
text: Sets many blocks at once, live, stored and sent; the cheapest way. A row takes `skin` too, for a player head. world.set_blocks(changes: { { at: Vec3, block: BlockRef, skin: HeadSkin ? } }) changes

title: World.spawn
text: Puts an entity at a point and returns its handle. A mob kind of the game by name (`world.spawn("cow", pos)`) is the game's own entity, and takes no `data`. A pack's own kind takes the data it starts life holding. `nil` for a kind nothing defined and this game does not have. world.spawn(def: EntityDef | string, pos: Vec3, data: { [string]: any }?) → EntityHandle ? def pos data

title: World.spawn_point
text: Where players arrive in this room; writable. The same value as the room's `spawn_point`. world.spawn_point: Vec3

title: World.time
text: Holds the sky at a time (ticks, or "sunrise", "day", "noon", "sunset", "night", "midnight"), or asks a function each tick, `s` seconds after the call. With no argument: the time of day now, 0 to 23999. world.time((at: number | TimeName | (s: number) -> number | TimeName) -> ()) → & (() -> number) (at

title: World.zone
text: Makes a box of blocks, both corners included, that knows who is in it; checked once a tick by feet position. Ends with the script. world.zone(opts: { from: Vec3, to: Vec3, on_enter: ((player: Player) -> ())?, on_leave: ((player: Player) -> ())? }) → Zone opts

title: Zone.contains
text: Returns true when the player is in the zone. zone:contains(player: Player) → boolean player

title: Zone.destroy
text: Removes the zone. zone:destroy()

title: Zone.players
text: Returns who is in the zone now. zone:players() → { Player }

title: citadel.budget
text: This pack's slice of a tick, and what it did with it. citadel.budget() → Budget

title: citadel.env
text: "development", "unlisted" or "published": which copy of the game this is. citadel.env: string

title: citadel.game
text: The game version from citadel.yml, e.g. "1.8.9". citadel.game: string

title: citadel.log
text: Writes its arguments to the server log, under this pack's name. citadel.log(... any) ...any

title: citadel.on_slow
text: Called when a batch runs out of budget; at most once a second. citadel.on_slow(fn: (slow: Slow) -> ()) → Connection fn

title: citadel.version
text: The engine version, e.g. "0.1.0". citadel.version: string

title: color.gradient
text: The colour `u` (0 to 1) of the way along the list; with `loop`, `u` wraps and the last colour runs back into the first. color.gradient(list: { Ink }, u: number, loop: boolean ?) → Color list u loop

title: color.hsv
text: Makes a colour from hue, saturation and value, each 0 to 1. color.hsv(h: number, s: number, v: number) → Color h s v

title: color.nearest
text: The colour a picture really shows, since it snaps to the map palette. color.nearest(c: Color) → Color c

title: data.copy
text: A detached JSON snapshot as ordinary Lua values/tables. data.copy(value: any) → any value

title: data.insert
text: Insert into a nested data list; omitted index appends. data.insert((list: DataView, value: any) -> ()) → & ((list: DataView, index: number, value: any) -> ()) (list

title: data.remove
text: Remove and return a detached value; omitted index removes the last element. data.remove(list: DataView, index: number ?) → any list index

title: fields.cells
text: A scattered grid, one point per `size` blocks: the distance to the nearest point, and that point's own number 0..1. fields.cells(size: number, seed: number ?) → { distance: Field, random: Field } size seed

title: fields.depth
text: Blocks under the surface: `fields.height - fields.y`. fields.depth: Field

title: fields.hash
text: One number 0..1 for each square of `cell` blocks (1). fields.hash(cell: number ?, seed: number ?) → Field cell seed

title: fields.height
text: The y of the surface of a column, as a block. fields.height: Field

title: fields.mix
text: `a` where `t` is 0, `b` where it is 1. fields.mix(a: Field | number, b: Field | number, t: Field | number) → Field a b t

title: fields.noise
text: Smooth noise, about -1..1. `solid = true` changes with y too. fields.noise(opts: { seed: number ?, scale: number ?, octaves: number ?, gain: number ?, lacunarity: number ?, solid: boolean ? }?) → Field opts

title: fields.room
text: The height of the open space a block is in: 0 in rock, 64 at most (and in the open sky). `density` cannot use it. fields.room: Field

title: fields.shore
text: 1 on a column at the water's edge with water beside it. fields.shore: Field

title: fields.slope
text: The step to the steepest of the four columns beside this one. fields.slope: Field

title: fields.water
text: How deep the water is over the surface; 0 and below on land. fields.water: Field

title: fields.x
text: fields.x: Field

title: fields.y
text: fields.y: Field

title: fields.z
text: fields.z: Field

title: http.get
text: GET a URL. `cache` is the seconds a 200 answer is kept on disk; `timeout` is 1 to 60 seconds, 15 by default. http.get(url: string, options: {query: {[string]: string }?, headers: {[string]: string }?, timeout: number ?, cache: number ?}?) → HttpResponse url options

title: http.socket
text: Opens a WebSocket (`ws` or `wss`) and keeps it open: when the connection ends, the engine dials again. `on_message` gets each message on a tick. http.socket(url: string, options: {headers: {[string]: string }?, on_message: (message: SocketMessage) -> ()}) → Socket url options

title: hub.experiences
text: The portals of the experience grounds. `experience` is what `/play` takes. hub.experiences() → { {slot: number, experience: string, title: string, pitch: string ?, icon: string ?, banner: string ?, players: number ?} }

title: hub.hubs
text: Every hub that is online, this one included. `id` is what `player:connect` takes. hub.hubs() → { {id: string, name: string, players: number ?, region: string ?} }

title: hub.point
text: Turns the player's own live portal to another published experience. hub.point(player: Player | string, slot: number, experience: string) → boolean player slot experience

title: hub.rent
text: Offers portal `slot` for Gems, to lead to `experience` (what `/play` takes). Returns the request id, or nil. More time on your own portal may leave `experience` out. hub.rent(player: Player | string, slot: number, product: string, experience: string ?) → string ? player slot product experience

title: hub.servers
text: The players' servers that are online, and the published experiences (`category == "experience"`). `id` is what `player:connect` takes. hub.servers() → { {id: string, name: string, category: string, motd: string ?, icon: string ?, banner: string ?, players: number ?, maxPlayers: number ?} }

title: models.new
text: Makes a model named `name` from the parts `fn` builds and returns it. Call it at the top of the script; from a callback it is an error. models.new(name: string, fn: (m: ModelBuild) -> ()) → Model name fn

title: network.find
text: The instance to send `players` players to (1 unless set), or nil when none has room. With `start`, one is started when none has room. network.find(options: {label: string, players: number ?, party: (Player | string)?, start: {member: string, slots: number, data: any }?}) → (NetworkStarted ?, string ?) options

title: network.info
text: This server's network, by name, and the instance this pack runs on: `id` and the fields after it are nil on a server that is not one. network.info() → ({network: string, id: string ?, member: string ?, label: string ?, slots: number ?, data: any }?, string ?)

title: network.list
text: The network's instances, or only those with `label`. network.list(label: string ?) → ({ NetworkInstance }, string ?) label

title: network.on_gone
text: Called with the id of an instance that is gone. network.on_gone(handler: (id: string) -> ()) → Connection handler

title: network.on_instance
text: Called when an instance starts or changes. network.on_instance(handler: (instance: NetworkInstance) -> ()) → Connection handler

title: network.start
text: Starts an instance of `member`. Answers at once; it is online later. network.start(options: {member: string, label: string, slots: number, data: any }) → (NetworkStarted ?, string ?) options

title: network.status
text: Says where this instance is. At most one a second is sent: the first at once, then the last of those that came after. network.status(options: {open: number, status: string ?, meta: any }) options

title: network.stop
text: Stops an instance of this network. network.stop(id: string) → (boolean, string ?) id

title: noise.new
text: Returns a noise. `scale` is the size of a hill in blocks (64), and each of the `octaves` (1) adds detail `lacunarity` (2) times finer and `gain` (0.5) times as strong. noise.new(opts: { seed: number ?, scale: number ?, octaves: number ?, gain: number ?, lacunarity: number ? }?) → Noise opts

title: parts.define
text: Declares a named part and its generator; nothing runs on load. A generator runs on request, or when its code changes. parts.define(def: PartDefinition) def

title: rooms.create
text: Creates an isolated room with its own chunks, players and effects; `spawn_point` defaults to (0.5, 65, 0.5), `generate` fills each chunk. rooms.create(opts: { spawn_point: Vec3 ?, generate: ((chunk: Chunk) -> ())? }) → Room opts

title: rooms.main
text: The main room, whose tables are the globals `world`, `players`, `ui` and the rest. rooms.main: Room

title: routes.add
text: From one dimension to another: standing `ticks` ticks in `block`, or only by `player:travel` without a trigger; arriving at `placement` or the destination's spawn. routes.add(route: { from: string, to: string, trigger: { block: string, ticks: number ? }?, placement: Vec3 ? }) route

title: shop.on_declined
text: Called when the player said no or did not answer. shop.on_declined(handler: (purchase: ShopPurchase) -> ()) → Connection handler

title: shop.on_paid
text: Called once per paid purchase; returning without an error hands it over. An error leaves it waiting, to be called again later. shop.on_paid(handler: (purchase: ShopPurchase) -> ()) → Connection handler

title: shop.owns
text: Whether the player owns this pass. shop.owns(player: Player | string, product: string) → boolean player product

title: shop.prompt
text: Asks Minefort to offer `product` to the player. Returns the request id, or nil when it was not offered. shop.prompt(player: Player | string, product: string) → string ? player product

title: storage.flush
text: Yields until saved; raises an error on failure. After initialization only. storage.flush()

title: storage.get
text: Returns the value saved under `key`, or nil when there is none. storage.get(key: string) → any key

title: storage.keys
text: Every key, sorted; with a prefix, only those that start with it. storage.keys(prefix: string ?) → { string } prefix

title: storage.set
text: Saves a value under `key` in this pack's storage.json; nil forgets it. storage.set(key: string, value: any) key value

title: storage.status
text: Last persistence error and whether there are unsaved changes. storage.status() → { pending: boolean, error: string ? }

title: stores.blob_list
text: Lists a player's blobs across all blob stores in this scope, each with its store, key, version and size. stores.blob_list(owner: string) → {{store: string, key: string, version: number, size: number }} owner

title: stores.lease
text: Takes a lease on `key` for `holder`, lasting `ttl_ms` milliseconds (up to one hour); returns a fencing token. stores.lease(key: string, holder: string, ttl_ms: number) → number key holder ttl_ms

title: stores.open
text: Returns the experience's one store. It takes no id; passing one is an error. stores.open() → DurableStore

title: stores.release
text: Gives up the lease on `key` that `token` holds. stores.release(key: string, token: number) key token

title: stores.renew
text: Extends the lease on `key` that `token` holds. stores.renew(key: string, token: number) key token

title: stores.request
text: Sends one raw query to the store and yields until it answers; returns the answer table and any blob bytes. stores.request(query: {[string]: any }, bytes: string ?) → ({[string]: any }, string ?) query bytes

title: time.every
text: Calls `fn` every `seconds`, precise to 1 ms and never drifting; use it for music. time.every(seconds: number, fn: () -> ()) → Connection seconds fn

title: time.now
text: Seconds since the pack started. time.now() → number

title: time.on_tick
text: Calls `fn` every tick, 20 times a second, with the tick number; keep it short. time.on_tick(fn: (tick: number) -> ()) → Connection fn
